context.summary: A compact hill-clan redoubt perched atop the chalk bluffs of the Undulating Downs, protected by timber palisades and surrounded by pastoral sheep-runs.
context.host_region_lore: Vast rolling hills of wild rye and fescue interrupted by craggy limestone bluffs, now echoing with the horn-calls of pastoral hill-clans and the hearth-smoke of Dun Kestrel.
context.scale_profile: Small / Compact (Fledgling cluster. Small structural footprint with a high proportion of surrounding natural terrain, open yards, and frontier buffer.)

perimeters.description: Transition into host region (The Undulating Downs — Hills).
perimeters.lore: Vast rolling hills of wild rye and fescue interrupted by craggy limestone bluffs, now echoing with the horn-calls of pastoral hill-clans and the hearth-smoke of Dun Kestrel.

approaches.road_lore: A beaten dirt and crushed-limestone track hacked through the western fringes of the Greenwood Vault, linking Dun Kestrel to the river wharf at Aethelford.
approaches.destination_lore: A pioneer river-haven and timber stockade founded on the western bank of the Silver Channel, guarding the primeval crossing into the Greenwood Vault.

context.world_relations: Dun Kestrel trades high-grade fleece, wool bales, salted mutton, and raw limestone along the Downs-Way to the river wharf at Aethelford, receiving Greenwood pine timber, river fish, and forged iron tools in return.
context.architectural_rationale: The heavy timber palisade crowns the upper slope to shield the central hearth and chieftain's lodge from steppe winds and raiders. The east gate opens directly onto the Downs-Way approach, placing the wool storehouse and craft smithy close to the gate for quick loading onto riverbound pack mules.

0.name: Frontier Buffer & Wild Downs
0.lore: Unzoned rolling hills of fescue, wild rye, and craggy limestone bluffs echoing with hill-clan horn calls.

1.name: Redoubt Commons & Hearth Yard
1.lore: The inner palisade enclosure centered around the ancient chalk hearth and hill smithy.

2.name: High Lodge Ward
2.lore: The sheltered southern wing housing the chieftain's timber hall and dry wool stores.

3.name: Pastoral Sheep-Runs & Terraces
3.lore: Enclosed hurdle pens and hillside sheep-runs where hill-clan flocks are folded and shorn.

4.name: Downs-Way Approach
4.lore: The beaten dirt and limestone track connecting the palisade threshold to Aethelford.

great_hearth.name: The Great Chalk Hearth
great_hearth.lore: A massive central hearth built from limestone slabs where clan elders gather to burn peat and brush, signaling distant downs.

clan_smithy.name: Kestrel Hill Smithy
clan_smithy.lore: A compact forge converting river-shipped iron ingots from Aethelford into sheep shears, palisade spikes, and hill-clan spears.

chieftain_hall.name: High Chieftain's Lodge
chieftain_hall.lore: A heavy timber-framed hall constructed from Greenwood pine bartered from Aethelford, serving as the clan seat and council chamber.

wool_storehouse.name: Downs Wool & Supply Vault
wool_storehouse.lore: A sturdy thatched storehouse filled with dense wool bales and salted mutton packaged for shipment along the Downs-Way.

sheep_fold.name: East Terraced Sheepfold
sheep_fold.lore: Woven hurdle enclosures holding hardy hill sheep whose high-grade fleece forms Dun Kestrel's primary export.
